title: Red Sea / Jeddah Corridor — Priced-Per-Fact Country Note
epistemic_framing: Provenance & confidence audit only: reports what purchased Telegraph inputs observed and where they contradict reported claims. Never asserts a definitive verdict on a live conflict.

reported_claim.summary: Regional freight circular claims normal port dwell times (<15h) at Jeddah with no active disruption reports.

observed.claim: Commercial container traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb strait experienced rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope in 2024-2026
observed.reasoning: No credible source found in the searches directly confirms or refutes this claim. It is left Unverified rather than guessed at; lack of evidence does not mean the claim is false.
sources: Maritime Disruption 2026: Red Sea, Suez and Hormuz Impact on Ocean Freight
Cape of Good Hope Route: +14 Days, and What It Cannot Replace | Straits

observed.answer: As of November 2026, Jeddah Islamic Port experiences vessel waits of five to ten days and release times of six to eight days due to Q4 import surges and war-related disruptions. King Abdullah Port serves as the main alternative for rerouting dry cargo without changing contract terms.
